headline: Nasdaq-100 weekend halt: Tail stays low after Friday's record probe was fully retraced, while a long end that rose on soft payrolls, triple-digit Brent and a third Gulf carrier group keep Stress elevated
body: Every hour of this published window falls inside the CME equity-index weekend halt. Index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about nine hours after the final published slot, so there is no tradeable session in which sustained mean-reversion failure could occur. Tail is therefore scored at 3 and stays between 2 and 4 across the whole forecast. The newest observable NQ structure is Friday's session. The index printed an intraday record of 31,017.53, then retraced roughly 210 points to close at 30,807.93, just above the 30,737.07 session low, for a 1.00% gain. A record probe that is given back into the close is a mean-reverting outcome, not the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that this framework requires before Tail approaches the watch band. The driver was the September employment report: 29,000 jobs against about 90,000 expected, unemployment up to 4.2% from 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.1% month over month. Priced odds of an October rate hike fell to roughly 16% from about 64% a week earlier. Semiconductors and megacaps led the advance and VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.6%, inside a narrow 15.30-16.24 range. Stress stays elevated at 52 rather than following VIX lower because the rate channel did not confirm the equity rally. The 10-year initially fell as much as 8bp on the weak payrolls print and then reversed to close up 4bp at 5.28%, with the 30-year at 5.61% and the 2-year at 4.84%. A long end near multi-decade highs that rises on dovish employment data points to fiscal and energy supply concerns rather than growth, and that divergence is unresolved going into the restart. Energy and geopolitics round out the Stress case. Brent held near $102.25 while WTI fell 1.9% to $91.11, with a G7 agreement to release up to 100 million barrels of reserves over four months offsetting a reported Chinese halt to fuel exports this month. The Gulf file was quiet in kinetic terms: the Day 218 update recorded no new escalation, a 26th consecutive period without coalition strikes on Iranian territory and a 24th day without Iranian ballistic launches at host states, the longest such interval of the resumed conflict. Posture nonetheless firmed, with a third carrier strike group deploying toward more than 20,000 personnel in theatre by month end, and regional exports running near 21.8 million barrels daily against 23.3 million before the war. Confidence is 86. Current levels for the index, VIX, the 2-year, 10-year and 30-year, crude and the seven-day U.S. calendar were all verified against primary or reputable current sources, and one conflict over Friday's 10-year close was resolved in favour of two concurring sources. The binding limitation is structural rather than evidential: no live NQ price path exists anywhere in this window, and the shared Finviz context was unusable, reporting partial collection status from 29 September with its futures and calendar sections unavailable. Independent research was used throughout in its place.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the final seven hours of Friday's payroll session and the first seventeen hours of the weekend halt. The window opens at its most defensive point: Tail 27 with an orange BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES state at 14:00Z, published while the index was extending toward its intraday record on a trend-up read shortly after the 13:30Z cash open. From 15:00Z onward the record probe was progressively given back and the mode moved to mixed, with Tail easing to 21-23 and a yellow WATCH state holding through 20:00Z. Once futures closed at 21:00Z, Tail dropped to 14 and then decayed steadily through the halt to 3 by 13:00Z, with the mode settling at normal from 00:00Z. Stress declined across the same span from 79 to 53 as realised volatility drained out of the closed market, while Confidence held between 82 and 89 throughout. All 24 slots are available from published Claude history and are preserved as originally assessed.
outlookSummary: All 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME weekend halt: index futures closed on Friday at 21:00Z and do not restart until 22:00Z on Sunday, about nine hours beyond the final published slot. With no tradeable session anywhere in the window there is no mechanism for sustained mean-reversion failure, so Tail is projected to stay between 2 and 4 and the mapped policy state remains EA_ON green throughout. Tail is held at 3 through Saturday afternoon, eases to 2 across the deepest part of the halt where the restart is furthest away, then lifts to 4 over the final hours as the distance to price discovery shortens and unpriced weekend information accumulates. Stress eases from 52 to 49 overnight as Friday's volatility decay carries forward, then firms back to 55 into Sunday as the catalyst load ahead of the restart builds: the OPEC+ online meeting reviewing November output targets, the unresolved divergence between a record equity close and a rising long end, and any weekend development in the Gulf. Confidence declines gradually from 86 to 78, reflecting only the ageing of the verified evidence base, since no fresher NQ price path can be gathered until futures reopen beyond this horizon. The first scheduled catalysts after the restart are ISM Services on 5 October at 14:00Z and the September FOMC minutes on 7 October at 18:00Z, both outside this window. No danger window is published, because a danger window inside a market-wide halt would not describe a tradeable risk.
